title: Hippocampal sharp-wave ripples correlate with periods of naturally occurring self-generated thoughts in humans | Nature Communications
abstract:
Buzsáki, G. Hippocampal sharp wave-ripple: a cognitive biomarker for episodic memory and planning.
Core features of human cognition highlight the importance of the capacity to focus on information distinct from events in the here and now, such as mind wandering. However, the brain mechanisms that underpin these self-generated states remain unclear. An emerging hypothesis is that self-generated states depend on the process of memory replay, which is linked to sharp-wave ripples (SWRs), which are transient high-frequency oscillations originating in the hippocampus.
Whether and how sharp-wave ripples (SWRs) accompany mental states that are less closely linked to events in the immediate environment are not fully understood. Here authors recorded SWRs from hippocampus of 10 epilepsy patients for up to 15 days with experience sampling.
